proposed_widenings.name: magic_item_stored_spell_reservoir
proposed_widenings.justification: The Reserve variant is not a passive grant, standard activation, triggered reaction, or spawned-creature item. It stores arbitrary incoming spells cast into the stone, tracks occupied spell-level capacity, and later releases one stored spell using the original caster's slot/DC/attack/spellcasting ability. That requires a dedicated storage/release item subgraph rather than coercing it into grant_spell_access or charge_pool.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "This vibrant purple prism stores spells cast into it, holding them until you use them. The stone can store up to 4 levels of spells at a time."

proposed_widenings.name: passive_metabolic_suppression
proposed_widenings.justification: The Sustenance variant grants a persistent no-food/no-water benefit while orbiting. No existing effect atom or passive operation expresses removing the need to eat or drink.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "You don't need to eat or drink while this clear spindle orbits your head."

proposed_widenings.name: triggered_reaction_progress_resource
proposed_widenings.justification: Absorption and Greater Absorption cancel triggering spells, but their burnout tracks cumulative absorbed spell levels across uses. Current activation resources are consumed-on-use pools with reset cadences, not monotonic lifetime intake tracked from trigger context.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "Once the stone has canceled 20 levels of spells, it burns out, turns dull gray, and loses its magic."

notes: Several variants fit individually as passive or triggered-reaction items: Agility/Fortitude/Insight/Intellect/Leadership/Strength, Awareness, Mastery, Protection, and Regeneration. The collection as a whole does not fit honestly because Reserve forces a missing storage/release family, Sustenance forces a missing passive effect, and the absorption variants also need trigger-context lifetime progress tracking. No content/tracer files were authored.
